name: Jira
description: Let agents search, read and work on issues in the Jira projects you choose.
identity: An Atlassian service account named "{brand.microsoft.appName}". It uses no Jira seat.

setup.title: Create a service account with Jira access
setup.body: In Atlassian Administration, create a service account named "{brand.microsoft.appName}". When it asks you to select an app role, set Jira to User and leave every other app, including Jira Administration, on None. Without a Jira role the account cannot use Jira at all.
click: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > Create service account
Select app role: Jira > User (every other app, including Jira Administration: None) > Create

setup.title: Add it to the projects agents should work in
setup.body: How you do this depends on the project. In a team-managed project (the usual kind on the Free plan), add the service account as a Member: Members can browse, comment on, move and create issues, and Viewers can only read. In a company-managed project on Standard or Premium, give it a project role whose permissions include the ones below. Without Browse projects the projects are listed but their issues stay hidden. You can narrow each agent to specific projects here later.
click: Team-managed project: the project > Project settings > Access > Add people > {brand.microsoft.appName} > Role: Member > Add
Company-managed project: the project > Project settings > People > Add people > {brand.microsoft.appName} > a role with the permissions below

setup.title: Create OAuth 2.0 credentials
setup.body: On the service account, select Create credentials, then OAuth 2.0, and select exactly these scopes. Copy the client ID and secret: Atlassian shows the secret only once.

fields.label: Jira site
fields.help: The part before .atlassian.net in your Jira address.

capabilities.label: Read issues
capabilities.description: Search and read issues and list projects.

capabilities.label: Comment
capabilities.description: Add comments to issues. In a service project a comment is public (the customer is emailed) unless the agent marks it as an internal note.

capabilities.label: Move issues
capabilities.description: Move issues to another status, such as In Progress or Done.

capabilities.label: Create issues
capabilities.description: Create new issues in the allowed projects.

capabilities.label: Delete issues
capabilities.description: Delete issues for good. Jira cannot bring a deleted issue back.

limits.label: Projects
limits.help: Leave empty to allow every project the service account can see.

discover.label: Projects agents can see
discover.ifEmpty: The service account cannot browse any project yet, so agents will find no issues. Give it a role with Browse projects in each project agents need, then check again.

revoke: In Atlassian Administration, open Directory, then Service accounts, then {brand.microsoft.appName}, and revoke its credentials.
